records.ledger_reason: OWNER AMENDMENT 2026-09-05 (rubric v3.6), verbatim: "c3c should be an accepted caveat on all holdout years", set alongside "an ISO can stay calibrated even if it degrades on holdout years". Auto-applied: this is an OUT-OF-TRAINING year (validation or locked-test tier per scripts/lib/holdout_policy.tier_for_year) and the governance gate passes. ON A HOLDOUT YEAR THE LONE-FAILURE CONDITION DOES NOT APPLY -- C3c is accepted here whatever else the year does, so unlike the in-sample standing rule this caveat may sit beside other failing criteria. Those criteria still FAIL, are still reported at full magnitude, and still drive this year's determination; what changes is only that C3c is no longer counted as one of them. WHY THAT IS NOT AN ESCAPE HATCH: the lone-failure guard exists to stop C3c masking a second defect on the years the model is CERTIFIED on, and a held-out year is not a certification -- rule 22 makes it ITERABLE model-SELECTION evidence that can never be quoted as an out-of-sample skill number. The scarcity price tail is also the one criterion this model class is known not to form (energy-only LMP, no administrative scarcity adder), which the rubric already accepts in-sample. UNCHANGED: the C3c band, tier and reported magnitude; the governance guard; the supporting-tier fail-closed guard; never a PASS (C3c reads CAVEAT, so grade_summary.target_grade never absorbs it); and both caveat budgets, which are checked first -- caveats aggregate PER CRITERION, so C3c failing on several holdout years is still one ledgered caveat.

ledger_entries.metric: hours RT-expressible LMP > $200/MWh (C3c scarcity tail, actual RT hourly gate; Indiana Hub)
ledger_entries.magnitude: model 0h [energy-only LMP] vs RT actual 30h (0.00×, >$200) (RE-MEASURED on closeout_miso_nuc_span by promote_keeper.py 2026-10-03; carried from 2026-10-02-w0-miso-fix2)
ledger_entries.classification: MODEL MISS (structural - MISO administrative ORDC/RCPF scarcity tail, not an emergent marginal-cost outcome even in MISO's own SCED; representation-frontier caveat, every admissible mechanism tried on record per rule #1)
ledger_entries.reason: MISO's real scarcity tail is an administrative stepped ORDC/RCPF curve DERIVED FROM a Monte-Carlo LOLP simulation over 10-30 min net-load/outage uncertainty (MISO Scarcity Pricing White Paper Mar-2024 §3.2.1; energy steps $1,100/$2,100 anchored to $3,500 VOLL, per-product reserve curves, BPM-002 Att.B §5.4; Potomac Economics IMM 2024 MISO SOM; OSTI 2424806). It prices probabilistic short-term risk a deterministic perfect-foresight hourly LP does not contain; the generic PCM literature confirms deterministic LPs systematically under-produce the spike tail (arXiv 2101.02303, 23/23-model survey; PyPSA-Eur arXiv 2606.16486). Empirical confirmation on the miso-81 keeper's OWN hourly output: in the 88 actual 2025 Indiana-Hub RT>$200 hours the model prices ~$50 median / $157 max, the reserve adder fires 2/88, energy+reserve>$200 in 1/88, zero load-shed; those hours are mostly low in the DA market (e.g. RT $1,598 / DA $99), and a deterministic LP ~= the DA market, so it cannot manufacture them. Reaching the tail would require MANUFACTURING the uncertainty (rules #1/#10 forbid the fitted path); layering an ORDC/RCPF adder would fire ~2 hours, not the actual count. Frontier designation 2026-07-20: every named admissible mechanism tried on record and adopted (reserve deliverability / 10-min ramp caps miso-39; Midwest sub-regional reserves miso-71; measured reserve requirements miso-56); further work needs a NEW admissible measured identification, its own charter. NEVER an offer adder tuned to the tail. See docs/multi-iso/miso-scarcity-tail-external-validation-2026-07.md + docs/multi-iso/miso-scarcity-tail-diagnosis.md.
ledger_entries.magnitude_basis: this run's own scored value (miso-268); the classification and reason are the standing MISO adjudication carried forward
